An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
